raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

With Model Runner V2, `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` / `VLLM_RAISE_ON_LOGIT_NANS` attribute NaN counts to the wrong requests whenever a request has more than one logits row (speculative decoding, or `num_new_sampled_tokens_per_step > 1`). `get_num_nans` counts NaNs per logits row and `AsyncOutput` zips that array with `req_ids`, so request `j` gets row `j`'s count and rows past `num_reqs` are dropped. This PR makes `get_num_nans` return one count per request.

Related: #63811 notes this as a separate bug (that issue was closed by the unrelated #63827). #38506 fixed it together with a dict-to-ndarray refactor for MRV1 and MRV2 and was closed by the stale bot on 2026-11-01 without merging. This PR is a minimal MRV2-only fix.

## Claims

- `SamplerOutput.num_nans` is `[num_reqs]` on every MRV2 path (`Sampler`, `RejectionSampler`, TP batch-shard gather), so `num_nans_in_logits`, `vllm:corrupted_requests` and `VLLM_RAISE_ON_LOGIT_NANS` see each request's own count.
- No host sync is added; the per-request sum happens in the Triton kernel, keyed by the on-device `input_batch.cu_num_logits`.
- The kernel is not slower than the old per-row kernel in any of 40 measured shapes on a B300, and about 2-9x faster at up to 32 requests.

## Validation

Two new tests and one updated test:

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py -k "num_nans"
pytest -v -s tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py -k "logprobs_and_nans"
```

- `test_get_num_nans_sums_rows_per_request` (new): per-request sums over `cu_num_logits` rows, padding rows ignored, a multi-row layout without drafts, and a vocab spanning several kernel chunks (NaNs on chunk edges, fp32 and bf16).
- `test_rejection_sampler_reports_num_nans_per_request` (new): `RejectionSampler.__call__` returns `[3, 1, 0, 17]` for 4 requests with `[3, 1, 4, 2]` rows. It reuses this file's existing harness.
- `test_gather_sampler_output_logprobs_and_nans` (updated): the sharded gather now receives per-request counts and copies them instead of reducing rows.

Results on 1x NVIDIA B300 with vLLM nightly `76c6f3f2a` (all touched files are identical to this branch's base):

```text
# main
FAILED test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py::test_get_num_nans_sums_rows_per_request
  TypeError: get_num_nans() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given
FAILED test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py::test_rejection_sampler_reports_num_nans_per_request
  assert [0, 1, 2, 1, 0, 0, ...] == [3, 1, 0, 17]   (10 per-row values)
FAILED test_gpu_batch_shard.py::test_gather_sampler_output_logprobs_and_nans[logprobs_dims0|1|2]
5 failed, 37 passed

# this PR
42 passed
```

`tests/v1/worker` with this PR: 712 passed, 0 failed. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the changed files.

There is no `LLM`-level test because producing NaN logits deterministically needs a test-only hook that writes NaN into KV blocks. We ran that check outside CI (below).

<details>
<summary>End-to-end check (Gemma-4-31B NVFP4, MTP 3, B300)</summary>

vLLM v0.28.0 (same code as main for the affected lines), MRV2, async scheduling, `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS=1`. After resetting the prefix cache, 5% of KV cache blocks were filled with NaN, then 13 req/s for 10 minutes. Ground truth for "this request had NaN logits" is an independent signal: the request was grammar-rejected into token 0. The per-request sum was applied as a monkeypatch around `RejectionSampler.__call__` (same semantics as this PR, not this kernel). The two rows are separate runs.

| | requests with NaN logits | flagged | correctly flagged | clean requests flagged |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main (per row) | 863 | 630 | 488 | 142 |
| per-request sum | 223 | 223 | 223 | 0 |

With the per-request sum, flagged = `vllm:corrupted_requests` = error-finished = grammar-rejected = 223.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Kernel benchmark: old per-row kernel vs this PR (B300, us per call)</summary>

`triton.testing.do_bench`, uniform rows per request. BLOCK_SIZE 2048 was chosen from a 2048/4096/8192 sweep: 4096 was 6% slower than the old kernel at 256 x 4 fp32, 2048 is not slower in any of the 40 shapes (worst case 69.8 vs 70.0 us).

| vocab, dtype | requests x rows | old | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 262144, fp32 | 1 x 1 | 89.6 | 10.2 |
| 262144, fp32 | 1 x 4 | 89.9 | 13.3 |
| 262144, fp32 | 32 x 4 | 100.6 | 36.3 |
| 262144, fp32 | 256 x 4 | 178.4 | 173.3 |
| 262144, bf16 | 32 x 4 | 64.7 | 24.6 |
| 262144, bf16 | 256 x 4 | 105.7 | 101.4 |
| 151936, fp32 | 32 x 4 | 61.9 | 27.7 |
| 151936, fp32 | 256 x 4 | 115.5 | 113.6 |

</details>

## Details

The rejection sampler is where this shows up in practice: it has `1 + num_draft` rows per request. `Sampler` had the same mapping problem when `num_new_sampled_tokens_per_step > 1` without drafts; with one row per request its result is unchanged. The TP batch-shard path already summed rows per request in `_pack_sampler_output_kernel`, so the two paths disagreed on what `SamplerOutput.num_nans` meant.

Fix:
- `get_num_nans(logits, cu_num_logits)` launches one program per (request, 2048-wide vocab chunk). Each program loops over that request's rows for its chunk and `tl.atomic_add`s into a zeroed `[num_reqs]` output. Integer atomics keep the count exact. Rows are clamped to `logits.shape[0]`.
- `Sampler` and `RejectionSampler` pass `input_batch.cu_num_logits`.
- The batch-shard pack kernel copies the per-request value and drops its `local_cu_num_logits_ptr` argument. `AsyncOutput` is unchanged.

Notes:
- The old kernel ran one program per row, which under-occupied the GPU for small batches. A first version with one program per request looping all rows was 2-4x slower at 4 rows per request and was dropped.
- The output needs `torch.zeros` (one extra memset) because chunks accumulate with atomics. This path is opt-in (`VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS`, off by default).
- MRV1 (`count_nans_per_row` / `nans_to_dict` in `gpu_model_runner.py`) has the same row-to-request mapping with spec decode. It is left unchanged to keep this PR MRV2-only; happy to follow up.
